title: Temple-portal /schedule accepts client-supplied ?slug= and any TEMPLE_MANAGER can overwrite any unlinked (org-less) temple's timingInfo
evidence: userCanEditTemple (lines 79-97): `async function userCanEditTemple(templeId, userId, hasManagerRole) { ... const orgId = rows[0]?.org_id; if (!orgId) return hasManagerRole; ... }` — i.e. when a temple has no org_id (legacy/unlinked), authorization collapses to the bare role flag. Schedule GET (203-222): `server.get<{ Querystring: { slug?: string } }>('/schedule', ... { const slug = request.query.slug; if (!slug) return 400; const temple = await prisma.temple.findUnique({ where: { slug }, ... }); ... }`. Schedule PATCH (224-254): `server.patch<{ Querystring: { slug?: string }; Body: unknown }>('/schedule', ... { const slug = request.query.slug; const tRow = await prisma.temple.findUnique({ where: { slug } }); ... await prisma.temple.update({ where: { slug }, ... timingInfo ... }); }`. Web page passes slug straight from the URL: apps/web/app/temple-portal/schedule/page.tsx `const s = params.get('slug') || localStorage.getItem('temple_portal_slug'); ... fetch(`/api/v1/temple-portal/schedule?slug=${encodeURIComponent(slug)}`)`.
impact: Any authenticated user holding the TEMPLE_MANAGER role can enumerate temple slugs and PATCH the timingInfo of ANY temple that has no org_id. timingInfo drives the public 'Live Darshan' / 'Next Aarti' badges, so an attacker can vandalize or deface live-darshan timings across the platform, or set bogus open windows. This is horizontal privilege escalation (manager A editing manager B's temple) plus integrity tampering of public-facing content. All other temple-portal endpoints (donations, pujas, darshan) correctly scope via resolveManagerTempleId(userId) — only the schedule endpoints are vulnerable, which matches the prior audit's localization.
repro: 1. Sign in as any TEMPLE_MANAGER whose own temple is irrelevant. 2. Pick any legacy temple slug T with no org_id (e.g. a temple created before the org linkage). 3. PATCH /api/v1/temple-portal/schedule?slug=T with body { regularHours: {Monday: '00:00 - 00:00'}, closedOn: 'all' }. 4. Server resolves tRow by slug, calls userCanEditTemple(T.id, userId, true) → orgId null → returns hasManagerRole=true → update succeeds. 5. Public temple page for T now shows corrupted timings.
suggestedFix: Remove the `if (!orgId) return hasManagerRole` legacy fallback. userCanEditTemple must return false whenever there is no org membership proving ownership — legacy unlinked temples should be migrated to an org (even a single-member org owned by their manager) or made admin-only editable. Additionally, do NOT accept the temple identity from the client query string: resolve the slug/id from request.currentUser via the manager's TempleProfile (resolveManagerTempleId already exists and is used by donations/pujas/darshan — reuse it for /schedule too).

title: temple-portal /schedule web page sends credentials:'include' with NO Authorization Bearer header — broken auth forwarding (401 for real users)
evidence: GET: `fetch(`/api/v1/temple-portal/schedule?slug=${encodeURIComponent(slug)}`, { credentials: 'include' })` — no headers. PATCH: `const res = await fetch(`/api/v1/temple-portal/schedule?slug=${encodeURIComponent(slug)}`, { method: 'PATCH', credentials: 'include', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: ... })` — no Authorization header. grep for useAuth/session/accessToken/token/Bearer/Authorization in the whole file returns EMPTY. Compare to every sibling temple-portal page: temple-portal/pujas `const token = session?.accessToken;`, temple-portal/donations `const token = session?.accessToken;`, temple-portal/darshan `const token = session?.accessToken;` — all send `Authorization: Bearer ${token}`. API authenticateUser only reads the Authorization header (middlewares/auth.ts:36-37 `function extractBearerToken(request) { const authHeader = request.headers.authorization; ... }`) and does NOT read the poojly_session cookie (grep for poojly_session/cookies across apps/api/src/middlewares + routes + lib = zero matches).
impact: The schedule editor is the only temple-portal page that omits the Bearer token. For any real (non-demo) temple manager, authenticateUser finds no Authorization header → 401 on both GET and PATCH, so the page can never load or save ('Failed to load schedule. You may not manage this temple.' toast fires on every visit). The feature is dead in production. This is a regression hiding behind B1: because the page never authenticates correctly, B1's IDOR is only practically reachable via a direct API call with a valid Bearer token (a logged-in TEMPLE_MANAGER hitting the endpoint through any other client), not via the broken web UI. Note the page also calls a relative `/api/v1/...` path (no API_BASE_URL) while siblings use `${API_BASE_URL}/...`, so it would only work if the API were same-origin — another sign the page was never wired up correctly.
repro: 1. Sign in as a real TEMPLE_MANAGER (Supabase JWT, not demo). 2. Open /temple-portal/schedule?slug=<own-temple>. 3. Browser network tab: GET /api/v1/temple-portal/schedule?slug=... returns 401 (no Authorization header sent, only cookies). 4. Form never populates; 'Failed to load schedule' toast appears. 5. Attempting Save also 401s.
suggestedFix: Mirror the sibling pages: pull `const { session } = useAuth(); const token = session?.accessToken;` and send `headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` }` on both fetches (drop `credentials:'include'` or keep it alongside the header). Use `${API_BASE_URL}` for the base path. Gate the effect on `if (!token) return;`. Then, after fixing auth forwarding, fix B1 so the slug is resolved server-side rather than trusted from the URL.

title: apps/web has NO Next.js middleware — /admin/** (and all portal) pages are reachable by any user; admin role is enforced only client-side via AuthGuard
evidence: No apps/web/middleware.ts and no apps/web/src/middleware.ts exist (filesystem check: `ls apps/web/middleware.ts apps/web/src/middleware.ts` → No such file). admin/layout.tsx (96-100) wraps children in client AuthGuard: `export default function AdminRootLayout({ children }) { return ( <AuthGuard allowedRoles={['admin']}> <AdminLayoutInner>{children}</AdminLayoutInner> </AuthGuard> ); }`. AuthGuard.tsx (28-67) is 'use client' and does the redirect in a useEffect: `if (!isAuthenticated) { window.location.href = `/auth/login?redirect=...` } ... if (user && allowedRoles && !allowedRoles.includes(user.role)) { window.location.href = getRoleDashboardPath(user.role); }`. The admin subpages themselves mostly import AuthGuard/useAuth but rely on the layout's wrapper (e.g. approvals/page.tsx, leads, outreach, waitlist, ratings, metrics, agents import useAuth but NOT their own AuthGuard — they inherit the layout's client guard). settings/page.tsx and commissions/page.tsx import neither.
impact: All 14+ admin pages (/admin, /admin/users, /admin/approvals, /admin/leads, /admin/outreach, /admin/waitlist, /admin/support, /admin/ratings, /admin/commissions, /admin/subscriptions, /admin/revenue, /admin/reports, /admin/metrics, /admin/agents, /admin/settings) are server-rendered/200 for ANY visitor — logged-out or wrong-role — because nothing blocks the request at the edge. A non-admin who hits /admin/users receives the full HTML/JS bundle (the sidebar links, the page component code) before the client useEffect runs a window.location redirect. The actual admin DATA is still protected server-side (every apps/api admin route has preHandler [authenticateUser, requireRole('admin')], verified for admin.ts, admin-ops.ts, admin-queue.ts, admin-metrics.ts, admin-leads.ts, admin-roadmap.ts, admin-subscriptions.ts, admin-agents.ts, admin-gurukuls.ts, admin-lead-conversion.ts, admin-bookings.ts, admin-temples.ts, admin-content-queue.ts, admin-donations-export.ts, marketplace-v2 marketplaceAdminRoutes, outreachAdminRoutes, whatsappBroadcastRoutes), so this is a UI-surface / information-disclosure exposure rather than a data breach: the admin nav structure, sidebar labels, and page skeletons leak to unauthenticated users, and there is a brief flash of admin chrome before the client redirect. It also means a JS-disabled or slow client sees the admin shell indefinitely. Same pattern applies to gaushala-portal/layout.tsx (allowedRoles ['gaushala_manager']) and temple-portal/layout.tsx (['temple_manager']) — all portal gating is client-only.
repro: 1. Open an incognito browser (not logged in). 2. Navigate directly to https://darshya.online/admin/users. 3. Server returns 200 with the admin layout HTML (sidebar with Users/Approvals/Leads/etc. links rendered). 4. Only after hydration does AuthGuard's useEffect fire and redirect to /auth/login. 5. View page source (before JS) — admin nav labels are visible. A curl of the URL returns the shell HTML.
suggestedFix: Add apps/web/middleware.ts that reads the session cookie (poojly_session) on the server, parses the user role, and returns a 401/307 redirect for /admin/** unless role === 'admin' (and equivalent for /gaushala-portal/** → gaushala_manager, /temple-portal/** → temple_manager, /astrologer-portal/** → astrologer, /wellness-portal/** → wellness_instructor, /gurukul-portal/** → appropriate role). Keep AuthGuard as the client fallback, but make the edge middleware the authoritative gate so no admin HTML/JS reaches an unauthorized request. This also fixes the same exposure on the other portals.

title: apps/admin portal gated by a single shared ADMIN_DASHBOARD_TOKEN cookie with no per-user identity, rotation, or revocation; all API calls use one shared server bearer
evidence: apps/admin/middleware.ts:6-33 `const COOKIE_NAME = 'darshya_admin_session'; ... const expected = process.env.ADMIN_DASHBOARD_TOKEN; ... const presented = request.cookies.get(COOKIE_NAME)?.value; if (presented === expected) { return NextResponse.next(); }` — single env value, single cookie name, plaintext `===` compare (not timing-safe). apps/admin/lib/api.ts: `export function adminApiBearer() { const bearer = process.env.ADMIN_API_BEARER ?? process.env.ADMIN_API_TOKEN; ... return bearer; }` and `adminApiHeaders() { return { 'content-type':'application/json', authorization: `Bearer ${adminApiBearer()}`, ... } }` — every server-side API call from the admin app uses the SAME static bearer for every human operator. Comment in lib/api.ts:3-5 confirms the model: 'the admin Next.js app is gated by middleware.ts (darshya_admin_session cookie comparing to ADMIN_DASHBOARD_TOKEN). Once a request reaches a route handler we trust the caller, but the API still requires its own admin token.'
impact: Two compounding weaknesses. (1) Access control: anyone who learns the single ADMIN_DASHBOARD_TOKEN cookie value gets full admin-portal access; there is no concept of individual admin accounts, no per-user revocation, no rotation without changing the shared env and disrupting every operator simultaneously, and the cookie is a long-lived static secret shared by all admins. The comparison is also non-constant-time (`presented === expected`). (2) Auditability: because all API calls are made with one shared ADMIN_API_BEARER, the API cannot distinguish which human admin performed a given destructive action (role change, approval, payout, refund, content moderation, lead status flip) — every action is attributed to the same identity, defeating per-actor audit trails. This is an internal/admin-only surface so severity is LOW, but it is a real gap versus per-user authn.
repro: 1. As any operator, set cookie darshya_admin_session=<ADMIN_DASHBOARD_TOKEN>. 2. Full admin portal opens. 3. Perform a destructive action (e.g. approve a provider, change a user's role). 4. API logs show the actor as the single shared admin bearer, not the individual — no way to tell which operator did it. 5. To revoke one compromised operator you must rotate ADMIN_DASHBOARD_TOKEN, kicking out every other admin too.
suggestedFix: Move apps/admin to per-user auth (reuse the same Supabase JWT + role system as apps/web) and add apps/admin/middleware.ts that verifies a real session and requireRole('admin'). Pass the individual operator's bearer through to the API instead of ADMIN_API_BEARER so the API's request.currentUser identifies the actor. If a shared-token model must stay short-term, at minimum: use timingSafeEqual for the cookie compare, set short expiry + HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite=Strict, support a token-rotation list (accept N most-recent tokens) for zero-downtime rotation, and log a stable operator id separately.

title: GAUSHALA_MANAGER portal has NO IDOR — all gaushala-portal API routes correctly scope by currentUser.id with ownership checks (no vulnerability; documented for completeness)
evidence: gaushala-portal.ts:20-34 GET /donations `if (!roles.includes('GAUSHALA_MANAGER')) return 403; ... const where = { gaushalaId: userId, ... }` (userId = request.currentUser!.id). :55-101 GET /dashboard scopes `gaushalaId: userId` and `findUnique({ where: { userId } })` for the profile. :130-157 PATCH /profile uses `findUnique({ where: { userId } })` / `update({ where: { userId } })`. gaushala-cows.ts:76-126 GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /cows/:id all do `const existing = await prisma.cow.findFirst({ where: { id, gaushalaId: gaushalaUserId } })` before any update/delete (gaushalaUserId = currentUser.id). gaushala-volunteers.ts:50-70 PATCH/DELETE /volunteers/:id same pattern: `findFirst({ where: { id, gaushalaId: gaushalaUserId } })` then update/delete. Web portal gated by gaushala-portal/layout.tsx AuthGuard allowedRoles ['gaushala_manager'] and pages send `Authorization: Bearer ${session?.accessToken}` (verified gaushala-portal/cows/page.tsx).
impact: Manager A cannot read or mutate manager B's gaushala profile, donations, cows, or volunteers — every query is filtered by gaushalaId = currentUser.id and every by-id mutation is preceded by an ownership findFirst. This is the correct pattern and contrasts sharply with the vulnerable temple-portal /schedule (B1). No privilege escalation or IDOR found in the gaushala domain.
repro: N/A — no vulnerability. (Negative result recorded so the coverage claim 'gaushala IDOR checked' is auditable.)
suggestedFix: No change required. Recommend applying this same resolve-by-currentUser + ownership-findFirst pattern to temple-portal /schedule to fix B1.

title: All apps/api admin*.ts routes verified to carry requireRole('admin') — no missing-guard privilege escalation found (negative result; documented for completeness)
evidence: Checked every listed admin route file for preHandler [authenticateUser, requireRole('admin')] (or token-gated cron equivalents): admin.ts, admin-ops.ts (GET ops routes use authorisedToken CRON_AUTH_TOKEN; POST /sla-overdue-bookings/resolve uses [authenticateUser, requireRole('admin')]), admin-queue.ts, admin-metrics.ts (authorised() = token OR admin-Bearer), admin-leads.ts (adminPreHandlers on all incl. PATCH /leads/:id/status, POST /leads/import, GET /cron/tick token-gated with timing-safe compare + header-preferred token), admin-roadmap.ts (`{ preHandler: [authenticateUser, requireRole('admin')] }`), admin-subscriptions.ts, admin-agents.ts (path-traversal protected: `/^[\w\-\d]+\.md$/` regex + `fpath.startsWith(REPORT_DIR)`), admin-gurukuls.ts, admin-lead-conversion.ts, admin-bookings.ts (adminPreHandlers on payouts/refunds/post actions), admin-temples.ts, admin-content-queue.ts (adminPreHandlers on all incl. /run, /auto-post, /generate), admin-donations-export.ts ([authenticateUser, requireRole('admin')]), marketplace-v2 marketplaceAdminRoutes (/keys POST/GET/DELETE all adminPreHandlers), outreach-webhook outreachAdminRoutes (/run /logs /config adminPreHandlers), whatsapp-broadcast whatsappBroadcastRoutes (adminPreHandlers). The only admin-namespaced routes NOT behind requireRole('admin') are token-gated cron/agent endpoints (admin-ops GETs, admin-metrics, admin-roadmap-orchestrator X-Orchestrator-Secret, admin-leads /cron/tick) which is the intended shared-secret model for GH-Actions callers.
impact: No privilege-escalation via a missing admin guard on the API. A non-admin JWT cannot reach any admin data-mutation route. The residual admin-surface weaknesses are the client-side-only web gating (B3) and the shared-token/no-per-user-identity model (B4), not missing API guards.
repro: N/A — negative result.
suggestedFix: No change required for the API guards. Note for hardening: the cron token-gated GETs (admin-ops, admin-metrics, admin-leads /cron/tick) accept the token via ?token= query (legacy) which can leak into Render access logs / CDN caches — admin-leads /cron/tick already prefers the x-cron-token header (P0 hardening comment); apply the same header-preferred pattern to admin-ops and admin-metrics token reads to keep the secret out of URLs.

title: Self-escalation check: PATCH /admin/users/:id role changes require admin and cannot be self-targeted to escalate — no self-escalation path found (negative result)
evidence: admin-api.ts patchUser: `export async function patchUser(token, userId, updates: { approved?, blocked?, roles?: BackendRole[] }) { const res = await fetch(`${API_BASE_URL}/admin/users/${userId}`, { method: 'PATCH', headers: { 'Content-Type':'application/json', ...authHeaders(token) }, body: JSON.stringify(updates) }) }` — always sends the caller's Bearer token. The receiving admin route requires [authenticateUser, requireRole('admin')], so a non-admin's token is 403'd before any role write. The users page (apps/web/app/admin/users/page.tsx) is wrapped by the admin layout's AuthGuard(['admin']) and only renders the role-change UI to admins. No endpoint allows a user to patch their OWN roles without already being admin (the guard precedes the mutation).
impact: A regular DEVOTEE/PANDIT/etc. cannot make themselves ADMIN: the role-change endpoint is admin-gated and the client that exposes it is itself admin-gated (client-side). There is no unauthenticated or self-targeted role-write path. (Caveat: the client-side gating in B3 means the role-change UI is *reachable* by a non-admin, but the actual mutation still requires a valid admin JWT on the API, so escalation does not succeed.)
repro: N/A — negative result.
suggestedFix: No change required beyond fixing B3 (so the role-change UI is not even rendered for non-admins). Additionally, consider an explicit server-side guard in the PATCH /admin/users/:id handler that forbids a user from modifying their own roles (defense-in-depth against a compromised admin locking in their own privilege), and log every role change with the actor identity — which requires B4's per-user bearer to be meaningful.

title: Video-call room URL has NO paid gate — logged-out user gets a free Jitsi consultation room with zero payment, zero auth, zero backend call
evidence: view/page.tsx Call button builds the room entirely client-side and navigates with no auth/payment: `const roomId = typeof crypto !== 'undefined' && 'randomUUID' in crypto ? crypto.randomUUID().replace(/-/g, '').slice(0, 24) : ...; const room = \`darshya-astrologer-${slug}-${roomId}\`; window.location.href = \`/consultation/${room}?provider=...\``. The room page consultation/[id]/page.tsx embeds Jitsi for ANY visitor with no check: `const jitsiUrl = \`https://meet.jit.si/${encodeURIComponent(room)}#config.prejoinPageEnabled=false...\`` then `<iframe allow="camera; microphone; fullscreen; display-capture; autoplay" src={jitsiUrl} .../>`. There is no AuthGuard, no consultation-status lookup, no payment verification.
impact: The entire paid astrology consultation flow is bypassable. A logged-out user (no account, no payment) clicks 'Call' on any astrologer profile and is dropped into a working HD video room with the astrologer's name. The paid /consultation/book + /verify-payment flow (Razorpay, ₹50 minimum, signature verification) is rendered pointless because the free path exists alongside it. Astrologers receive zero revenue for these calls. Also a privacy/safety issue: any internet user can open a room branded with a real astrologer's name and lure victims (impersonation).
repro: 1) Open incognito (not logged in). 2) Visit /astrology/view?id=astro_001. 3) Click 'Call' (green button, enabled when isOnline && !isBusy). 4) Landing on /consultation/darshya-astrologer-pt-raghunath-sharma-<id> embeds meet.jit.si and requests camera+mic — full video call, no login, no payment.
suggestedFix: Remove the client-side room-generation Call button, or route it through POST /consultation/start (which itself must add a paid/role gate — see AP-02). The /consultation/[id] room page MUST wrap in <AuthGuard> and, for paid consultations, verify server-side that the calling user owns a confirmed (paid) consultation whose room_name === id before embedding Jitsi. Mirror the success page (consultation/[id]/success/page.tsx) which already only reveals jitsiUrl when status==='confirmed'.

title: POST /consultation/start returns a Jitsi room URL to ANY authenticated user with no payment, no role check, no DB row — roomUrl leak
evidence: Route only has `preHandler: [authenticateUser]` (any logged-in user, any role). Comment admits the bypass: `// Ephemeral Jitsi room (kept for backward-compat — used by /astrology page "Call" button which spins a free-trial room w/o payment).` Body is unvalidated (`request.body ?? {}`). It returns `roomName`, `jitsiUrl`, `embedUrl` immediately: `return reply.send({ roomName, jitsiUrl: \`https://meet.jit.si/${roomName}#userInfo.displayName=...\`, embedUrl: ..., provider: 'jitsi', kind, createdAt: ... });`
impact: Any logged-in user (even a brand-new DEVOTEE with no astrologer role, no booking, no payment) can mint unlimited free video-call rooms for any astrologer/priest/wellness provider by POSTing {providerName: '...'} . The paid /consultation/book flow that charges ₹50+ and verifies a Razorpay signature is circumvented. This is the server-side twin of AP-01.
repro: curl -X POST $API/v1/consultation/start -H 'Authorization: Bearer <any-valid-token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"providerName":"Pt Raghunath Sharma","kind":"astrologer"}' → 200 with jitsiUrl. No payment, no booking row.
suggestedFix: Gate /consultation/start behind a confirmed (paid) consultation lookup: require a consultationId in the body, verify the caller owns a row with status='confirmed' (or 'completed' in-progress), and return only that row's stored room_name. Remove the free-trial room path or restrict it to ADMIN/demo mode only.

title: IDOR: PATCH /astrology/consultations/:id and POST /astrology/consultations/:id/start-call perform NO ownership check — any logged-in user can complete/cancel/start-call ANY consultation
evidence: Route layer passes only the id to the service with no caller binding: `server.patch('/consultations/:id', { preHandler: [authenticateUser] }, async (request, reply) => { const { id } = request.params as { id: string }; ... const updated = await astrologyService.updateConsultation(id, parsed.data.status); ... })` and `server.post('/consultations/:id/start-call', { preHandler: [authenticateUser] }, async (request, reply) => { const { id } = request.params; const result = await astrologyService.startCall(id); ... })`. Service methods ignore the caller entirely: `async updateConsultation(id, status) { const session = this.sessions.get(id); if (!session) throw new Error('Consultation not found'); session.status = ...; return session; }` and `async startCall(id) { const session = this.sessions.get(id); if (!session) throw new Error('Consultation not found'); if (!session.roomUrl) { session.roomUrl = \`https://meet.jit.si/darshya-${id}\`; session.status = 'in_progress'; } return { roomUrl: session.roomUrl }; }`. request.currentUser is read by the route for the auth prehandler but never used to authorize the action.
impact: A logged-in user A can complete or cancel user B's consultation ( PATCH /astrology/consultations/<B's session id> with {status:'COMPLETED'|'CANCELLED'} ) and can mint the Jitsi room for B's session ( start-call ). Session ids are `session_${Date.now()}_${6-char-base36}` — the Date.now() portion is enumerable and the random suffix is only ~36^6 ≈ 2B, plus the in-memory store is shared across all users. Lets a malicious user disrupt other users' consultations and harvest room URLs. The astrologer portal Consultations page (handleJoin/handlePatch) drives these endpoints.
repro: 1) As user A, start a consultation: POST /astrology/consult/start {astrologerId:'astro_001', mode:'video'} → note session id. 2) As user B (different account), PATCH /astrology/consultations/<A's session id> {status:'COMPLETED'} → 200 {consultation:{...status:'completed'}}. B just closed A's session. Same for start-call.
suggestedFix: Pass request.currentUser.id into updateConsultation/startCall and verify session.userId === caller.id (for devotee) OR session.astrologerId maps to caller (for astrologer) before mutating. Return 403 on mismatch. Mirror consultation.ts:481 which does `if (row.user_id !== request.currentUser!.id) return reply.code(403)...`.

title: Astrologer portal Consultations page is permanently empty — listConsultations filters by UUID but sessions store slug astrologerId, so the astrologer sees zero consultations
evidence: Service: `async listConsultations({ userId, role }) { const all = Array.from(this.sessions.values()); if (role === 'astrologer') return all.filter((s) => s.astrologerId === userId); return all.filter((s) => s.userId === userId); }`. startConsultation stores the slug, not the user UUID: `this.sessions.set(sessionId, { id: sessionId, userId, astrologerId, ... })` where astrologerId is the in-memory slug 'astro_001' (passed from the client). Route passes the caller's UUID as userId: `const userId = request.currentUser!.id; const role = (request.query).role ?? 'astrologer'; const consultations = await astrologyService.listConsultations({ userId, role });`. The UI calls with role=astrologer: `fetch(\`${API_BASE_URL}/astrology/consultations?role=astrologer\`)`. UUID !== 'astro_001' → filter returns [].
impact: The astrologer-portal/consultations page (the astrologer's session-management screen with Join/End/Cancel buttons) will ALWAYS render 'No upcoming consultations' / 'No past consultations' for any real logged-in astrologer. The astrologer cannot see or manage sessions assigned to them. Combined with AP-05, the entire astrologer portal consultations surface is dead.
repro: 1) Log in as astrologer (demo-astro-token or real astrologer account). 2) Open /astrologer-portal/consultations. 3) Even after a devotee starts a consultation with that astrologer via /astrology/consult/start, the page shows 'No upcoming consultations'. Network: GET /astrology/consultations?role=astrologer returns {consultations:[]}.
suggestedFix: Map the in-memory astrologer slug to the real User UUID (the deferred 'slug→User onboarding' pass the code comments keep deferring), OR have startConsultation store the resolved astrologer's userId when the caller is the astrologer. Short term: have listConsultations for role=astrologer also match on a slug↔user lookup table.

title: Astrologer dashboard earnings/consultations queries filter by UUID astrologer_id, but paid bookings store the slug — real astrologers see 0 earnings, 0 consultations, 0 upcoming sessions forever
evidence: Dashboard query filters by the caller's UUID: `SELECT COUNT(*)::text AS count, COALESCE(SUM(amount_inr),0)::text AS sum FROM astrologer_consultations WHERE astrologer_id = $1 AND status = 'confirmed' AND paid_at::date = CURRENT_DATE` with `userId` (UUID) bound to $1 (line 58). Same UUID filter for month/total/upcoming (lines 64-88). But the book flow inserts the slug: `INSERT INTO astrologer_consultations (reference, user_id, astrologer_id, astrologer_name, ...) VALUES ($1, $2::uuid, $3, $4, ...)` where `$3 = astrologerId` = parsed.data.astrologerId = the client-sent slug 'astro_001' (consultation.ts:166,223). The code's own comment acknowledges the mismatch but hand-waves it as 'intentional (demo data)' (astrologer-portal.ts:43-46) — it is NOT intentional for real bookings.
impact: Every confirmed, paid astrology consultation (via /consultation/book → /verify-payment) writes astrologer_id = 'astro_001' (slug). The astrologer's dashboard queries WHERE astrologer_id = <UUID>, so NONE of their real paid sessions ever appear. The astrologer sees earningsTodayInr=0, earningsMonthInr=0, totalEarningsInr=0, consultationsToday=0, upcomingSessions=[] permanently. Astrologers cannot see their real revenue or upcoming paid sessions. This is the same slug-vs-UUID gap as AP-04 but on the PAID path — meaning even genuinely paid consultations are invisible to the provider.
repro: 1) As a devotee, book + pay for a consultation with astro_001 via /consultation/book + /verify-payment (row inserted with astrologer_id='astro_001'). 2) Log in as the astrologer tied to astro_001. 3) GET /astrologer-portal/dashboard → stats.consultationsToday=0, totalEarningsInr=0, upcomingSessions=[] despite the paid confirmed row existing in the table.
suggestedFix: Resolve the slug→User UUID mapping at booking time (store the real astrologer User.id in astrologer_id, keep slug in a separate column for display), or change the dashboard WHERE clause to match on the slug via a join/lookup. The deferred 'real astrologer onboarding' pass is now blocking both earnings visibility (AP-05) and session management (AP-04).

title: Astrologer earnings from paid consultations NEVER create a Commission/payout row — earnings page is permanently 0 (same class as the priest createPriestPayout zero-callers bug)
evidence: consultation.ts /verify-payment flips status to 'confirmed' and mints a room but writes NO commission: `await prisma.$executeRawUnsafe(\`UPDATE astrologer_consultations SET status = 'confirmed', razorpay_payment_id = $1, room_name = $2, paid_at = now() WHERE id = $3::uuid;\`, razorpay_payment_id ?? null, roomName, consultationId);` — no prisma.commission.create anywhere in the file (grep confirms commission.create exists only in payment.service.ts:213 and booking.service.ts:314, both puja paths). booking.service.ts:304-323 shows the correct pattern for puja: `if (newStatus === 'confirmed') { ... await prisma.commission.create({ data: { bookingId: updated.id, providerId: updated.priestId, amount: updated.platformCommission, percentage, status: 'PENDING' } }) }`. The astrologer earnings page renders CommissionsPanel which reads ONLY the Commission table: `mode === 'admin' ? await listCommissions(...) : await listMyCommissions(...)` (CommissionsPanel.tsx:79-82) → GET /admin/commissions?providerId=me.
impact: The astrologer-portal Earnings page (and the dashboard EarningsCard) draw exclusively from the Commission ledger. Because no astrology consultation ever writes a Commission row, an astrologer's earnings are permanently ₹0 in the payouts UI regardless of how many paid consultations they complete. This is the exact 'createPriestPayout zero-callers' failure pattern, now on the astrology side: the payout/earnings surface is wired to a ledger that the consultation flow never feeds. Payout reconciliation is impossible for admins too (/admin/commissions will never list astrology revenue).
repro: 1) Complete a full paid consultation: devotee books + pays (Razorpay verify succeeds), admin marks /:id/complete. 2) Log in as the astrologer → /astrologer-portal/earnings → 'No commission records yet.' 3) As admin → /admin/commissions → no astrology row exists. The astrologer_consultations row is 'completed' with amount_inr set, but no Commission row was ever created.
suggestedFix: In consultation.ts /verify-payment (or /:id/complete), after flipping to confirmed/completed, write a prisma.commission.create with bookingId=consultation.id, providerId=resolved-astrologer-User-id, amount=platform commission (compute from amount_inr * platform rate), status='PENDING' — guarded by findFirst for idempotency, exactly as booking.service.ts:304-323 does for pujas.

title: Astrologer dashboard silently skips the API for demo sessions — demo astrologer sees hardcoded ZERO_STATS, never real data
evidence: `useEffect(() => { if (!session?.accessToken || session.accessToken.startsWith('demo-')) return; (async () => { try { const r = await fetch(\`${API_BASE_URL}/astrologer-portal/dashboard\`, { headers: { Authorization: \`Bearer ${session.accessToken}\` } }); ... })(); }, [session]);` The same demo-skip guard repeats for the KYC fetch (line 72). A demo astrologer token is `demo-astro-token` (auth-context.tsx:214 `accessToken: \`demo-${handle}-token\``), which starts with 'demo-'.
impact: The only way to log in as an astrologer in dev/staging/demo (demo-astro-token, astro@demo.com) makes the dashboard render ZERO_STATS (0 sessions, 0 earnings, '—' rating) and KYC 'unsubmitted' — the API is never called. Investors/devs testing the astrologer portal see an empty dashboard and assume the backend is broken or the astrologer has no activity, when in fact the client refused to fetch. Masks real backend bugs (AP-04/AP-05) during demo. Note: the demo token IS accepted by the API middleware (auth.ts:111 demoAllowed), so the fetch would work — the client just chooses not to.
repro: 1) Log in as demo astrologer (astro@demo.com / demo123, or demo-astro-token). 2) /astrologer-portal shows 0 everything + KYC unsubmitted. 3) Network tab: no GET /astrologer-portal/dashboard request is made.
suggestedFix: Remove the `session.accessToken.startsWith('demo-')` early-return (the API accepts demo tokens in non-prod). If demo must be visually distinct, fetch real data and overlay a 'demo data' badge instead of suppressing the call.

title: Assigned astrologer can NEVER mark their own consultation complete — /:id/complete requires ADMIN because astrologer_id (slug) can never equal currentUser.id (UUID)
evidence: Gate: `const isAdmin = roles.includes('ADMIN'); const isAssignedAstrologer = row.astrologer_id === request.currentUser!.id; if (!isAdmin && !isAssignedAstrologer) return reply.code(403).send({ error: 'Only the assigned astrologer or admin can mark complete.' });`. The code's own comment (lines 430-435) admits the gap: `// astrologer_id stores the in-memory astrology.service slug (e.g. 'astro_002'), not a User.id UUID, so equality with currentUser.id can never succeed for a real astrologer. ... until then only ADMIN can close the lifecycle.`
impact: The lifecycle close (confirmed → completed, which is what triggers payout eligibility and frees the astrologer) is admin-only in practice. The assigned astrologer cannot end their own session via the API — the portal Consultations page 'End' button (handlePatch) targets the in-memory /astrology/consultations/:id service instead, which doesn't touch the paid astrologer_consultations row at all. So paid consultations can only be completed by an admin manually via /admin/consultations, creating an ops bottleneck and leaving rows stuck in 'confirmed'.
repro: 1) As the astrologer tied to astro_001, call PATCH /consultation/<confirmed-consultation-id>/complete → 403 'Only the assigned astrologer or admin can mark complete.' 2) As admin → 200 completed.
suggestedFix: Resolve slug→User.id (same fix as AP-04/AP-05) so isAssignedAstrologer can be true for the real astrologer, OR add an explicit astrologer-self path that looks up the astrologer's profile by userId and matches on the slug stored in the row.

title: Astrologer portal profile 'Save Changes' sends pricePerMinute=0 as valid — astrologer can silently set their rate to ₹0/min (and the paid flow then rejects with ₹50 min, confusingly)
evidence: Schema allows 0: `pricePerMinute: z.number().min(0).max(100000).optional(),` (line 11). The UI clamps to >=0: `onChange={(e) => updateField('pricePerMinute', Math.max(0, parseFloat(e.target.value) || 0))}`. PATCH /profile accepts it: `const profile = await prisma.astrologerProfile.update({ where: { userId }, data: parsed.data });`. But the book flow (consultation.ts:176-183) computes `amountInr = Math.round(perMinuteRate * minutes)` and rejects `if (amountInr < 50) return reply.code(400).send({ error: 'Minimum consultation amount is ₹50.' })`.
impact: An astrologer can save pricePerMinute=0 (or any rate yielding <₹50 for the chosen minutes). Their profile shows ₹0/min, devotees book, but /consultation/book returns 400 'Minimum consultation amount is ₹50' — the booking silently fails at payment time with an error that doesn't explain the rate is the problem. Mismatched validation between profile-save and booking creates a broken astrologer listing.
repro: 1) As astrologer, set Per-Minute Rate = 0, Save → 200 OK. 2) As devotee, open /astrology/<id>/book, 15 min × ₹0 = ₹0, click Pay → 400 'Minimum consultation amount is ₹50.'
suggestedFix: Set pricePerMinute min to a positive floor (e.g. .min(1)) in profileUpdateSchema, and ideally enforce a minimum that aligns with the ₹50-amount rule (rate × minMinutes >= 50). Surface a clear error on the profile form if the rate is too low.

title: GET /consultation/:id (single consultation fetch) excludes astrologers/admins — assigned astrologer gets 403 reading their own consultation
evidence: Only the booking user is authorized: `if (row.user_id !== request.currentUser!.id) return reply.code(403).send({ error: 'Not authorized.' });`. There is no branch for the assigned astrologer (row.astrologer_id) or ADMIN. The success page (consultation/[id]/success) uses this endpoint, so an astrologer opening a success link gets 403.
impact: An astrologer who navigates to a consultation detail/success URL (e.g. via a notification or the admin share) is wrongly rejected with 'Not authorized' even though it is their own session. Admins must use /admin/all instead. Minor UX/auth gap; the astrologer already has /astrologer/mine for listing, but single-fetch is devotee-only.
repro: As the assigned astrologer, GET /consultation/<their-session-id> → 403 'Not authorized.'
suggestedFix: Allow the assigned astrologer (once slug→UUID resolved) and ADMIN: `const isAssignedAstrologer = row.astrologer_id === request.currentUser!.id; const isAdmin = roles.includes('ADMIN'); if (!isAssigned && !isAssignedAstrologer && !isAdmin) return 403;` and strip sensitive devotee fields (user_id) when the caller is the astrologer.

title: Astrology public list/detail pages render hardcoded fallback data and never call the API — profile edits (PATCH /astrologer-portal/profile) have zero effect on what devotees see
evidence: AstrologyClient.tsx initializes state from hardcoded `fallbackAstrologers` (lines 73-210) and never fetches /astrology/astrologers in a useEffect — the API client exists (astrologer-api.ts) but the list page doesn't use it for the cards. view/page.tsx uses a hardcoded `allAstrologers` record (lines 56-129) keyed by astro_001/002/003 and falls back to astro_001 for unknown ids: `const astrologer = allAstrologers[id] || allAstrologers['astro_001']!;`. Meanwhile the astrologer portal PATCH /astrologer-portal/profile updates the AstrologerProfile DB row (displayName, bio, specialties, pricePerMinute) — but that row is never read by either public page.
impact: An astrologer's profile edits (bio, specialties, per-minute rate, display name) saved in the portal are invisible to devotees — the public pages show the hardcoded demo data (Pt. Raghunath Sharma ₹50, etc.) regardless. A real astrologer onboarding and setting their rate to ₹75/min will still appear as ₹50/min to every devotee. The /astrology/astrologers API endpoint exists and returns the in-memory service list, but neither public page consumes it for the cards/detail, so there's a total disconnect between the provider-editable profile and the devotee-visible listing.
repro: 1) As astrologer, edit profile: change display name to 'Test Astrologer', rate to ₹75, Save → 200. 2) Open /astrology and /astrology/view?id=<your-id> → still shows hardcoded fallback (e.g. 'Pt. Raghunath Sharma', ₹50).
suggestedFix: Have AstrologyClient.tsx fetch GET /astrology/astrologers and view/page.tsx fetch GET /astrology/astrologers/:id on mount (with the existing hardcoded arrays as error fallback only). The in-memory astrology.service ASTROLOGERS list should itself be seeded from / be replaced by AstrologerProfile rows so portal edits propagate.

title: Priest verification gate is dead: PANDIT role + auto-created active Priest = any self-signup user becomes a verified priest
evidence: requireRole('priest') line 337: `if (userRoles.includes('PANDIT')) return;` — grants access on PANDIT role ALONE, BEFORE the status check at line 356 (`if (!priest || priest.status !== 'active')`). The status check is unreachable for PANDIT holders. getPriestId (priest.ts:75-86) auto-creates a Priest via `prisma.priest.create({ data: { userId, displayName, specializations, languages, experienceYears, bio } })` — it does NOT set status or verificationStatus, so schema defaults apply: `status @default(active)` (schema:305) and `verificationStatus @default(pending)` (schema:301). auth.ts:783-838 SIGNUP_ROLE_ENUM lets a user POST /signup with role:'pandit' → UserRoleAssignment.create({role:'PANDIT'}) with NO approval step.
impact: Any unauthenticated visitor can self-signup as role='pandit' (no approval), then call any /api/v1/priest/* endpoint: requireRole('priest') returns on PANDIT, getPriestId auto-creates an ACTIVE priest record, and they have full priest powers — accepting pujas, marking bookings complete, uploading video proof, (once payouts are wired) receiving payouts. The entire priest-verification/onboarding-approval model is bypassable. Logged-in impact; also degrades trust for logged-out devotees who assume priests are verified.
repro: 1. POST /api/v1/auth/signup {email, password, role:'pandit', fullName} → 200, UserRoleAssignment PANDIT created. 2. POST /api/v1/auth/login → token. 3. GET /api/v1/priest/dashboard → 200 (getPriestId auto-creates active Priest). 4. Accept/complete a booking via PATCH /api/v1/bookings/:id (see C1). Expected: signup-as-pandit requires admin approval; /priest/* requires status=active + verificationStatus=verified. Observed: full access immediately.
suggestedFix: Two-part: (a) requireRole('priest') — REMOVE the early `if (userRoles.includes('PANDIT')) return;`. Always run the priest-lookup + require `priest.status === 'active' && priest.verificationStatus === 'verified'`. Only ADMIN may waive. (b) Signup — do NOT let /signup self-assign any role other than DEVOTEE. A 'pandit' (or any provider) role request must create a Lead/Pending profile (onboarding.service.ts) and require admin approval before UserRoleAssignment is written. (c) getPriestId — do NOT auto-create an active Priest; if no Priest row exists, 403 'priest account not onboarded' (it should only be created by the onboarding/approval flow with status=pending). (d) Re-run priest.service tests + add: signup-as-pandit does NOT yield priest powers until admin approves.

title: No apps/web/middleware.ts — all 6 portal layouts gated client-side only; logged-out/non-role users receive the full portal HTML/JS shell before redirect
evidence: Confirmed no apps/web/middleware.ts. All portal layouts use <AuthGuard allowedRoles=[...]> which runs in a client useEffect — the server renders the portal shell (nav, sidebar, page chrome) to a 200 response, THEN the client checks the session and redirects. API routes remain protected (requireRole server-side), so no data leak, but the shell (nav labels, route structure, sometimes static placeholder text) is visible to anyone hitting /admin etc. directly.
impact: Logged-out or wrong-role users see a brief flash of the portal shell (nav/labels) on /admin, /priest, /store-admin, /astrologer-portal, /wellness-portal, /gaushala-portal before client redirect. No data exfiltration (API gated), but it leaks portal structure and is a poor auth boundary. Low severity; medium if any portal page hardcodes sensitive constants.
repro: 1. Open a fresh browser (no session). 2. Visit https://darshya.online/admin. Expected: server redirects to /auth/login before render. Observed: portal shell HTML renders (200), then client redirects.
suggestedFix: Add apps/web/middleware.ts that checks the session cookie/token and redirects unauthenticated/non-role users from /admin/**, /priest/**, /store-admin/**, /astrologer-portal/**, /wellness-portal/**, /gaushala-portal/** to /auth/login before the page renders. NOTE: memory reference_bhaktisetu_cf_pages_no_middleware says middleware.ts was a build-breaker on the OLD Cloudflare Pages deploy — but prod is now Render Node standalone (reference_darshya_cf_pages_next_on_pages_dead), so middleware is safe to add. Verify the build still passes.

title: Demo-token ADMIN bypass (demo-admin → ADMIN) — guarded by boot-fatal + prod reject, but a prod env misconfigure (ALLOW_DEMO_TOKENS=true) would re-arm it
evidence: DEMO_ROLE_MAP maps 'admin' → ['ADMIN','DEVOTEE'] (auth.ts:122). Defenses: line 98-99 `demoAllowed = NODE_ENV !== 'production' || ALLOW_DEMO_TOKENS === 'true'`; line 104 rejects demo tokens when !demoAllowed; line 11-15 boot-fatal: `if (ALLOW_DEMO_TOKENS==='true' && NODE_ENV==='production') process.exit(1)`. Same gate on /login demo accounts (auth.ts:645). DEPLOY.md:15 sets NODE_ENV=production.
impact: In correctly-configured prod (NODE_ENV=production, ALLOW_DEMO_TOKENS unset): demo-admin token is 401-rejected; cannot become admin. The bypass is only re-armed if an operator sets ALLOW_DEMO_TOKENS=true in prod — but the boot guard crashes the server first, so it cannot serve traffic. Defense-in-depth is strong. Low severity (residual misconfig risk only).
repro: 1. In prod (NODE_ENV=production, no ALLOW_DEMO_TOKENS): curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer demo-admin-...' /api/v1/admin/users → 401 'Demo tokens not accepted in production.' 2. If operator sets ALLOW_DEMO_TOKENS=true in prod → API process exits at boot (FATAL log).
suggestedFix: No code change needed (guards are correct). Defense-in-depth: add a deploy-time check / Render env validation that refuses ALLOW_DEMO_TOKENS=true in the prod service. Optionally add a test asserting the boot-fatal guard. Ensure ALLOW_DEMO_TOKENS is absent (not 'false') in prod env to avoid any string-truth edge.

title: Donation verify accepts any valid Razorpay signature; client razorpay_order_id never compared to donation row's order id; no ownership check
evidence: donations.ts:176-197 — `if (!isDemoPayment) { if (!body.razorpay_order_id || !body.razorpay_payment_id || !body.razorpay_signature) { return reply.code(400)... } const expected = crypto.createHmac('sha256', razorpayKeySecret).update(`${body.razorpay_order_id}|${body.razorpay_payment_id}`).digest('hex'); ... if (!sigOk) { ... return reply.code(400).send({ error: 'Invalid payment signature' }); } }` — the HMAC is computed over the CLIENT-SUPPLIED body.razorpay_order_id and compared to the client signature, but body.razorpay_order_id is NEVER compared to donation.razorpay_order_id (the row's stored order id). The donation is looked up ONLY by body.donationId (line 161-167). No check that request.currentUser.id === donation.user_id either. Compare consultation.ts:270 `if (row.user_id !== userId) { return reply.code(403)... }` and consultation.ts:288 `if (razorpay_order_id !== row.razorpay_order_id) { return reply.code(400).send({ error: 'Order id mismatch.' }); }` — both guards present in the consultation handler, both ABSENT in the donation handler.
impact: Forged payment confirmation / free donations. An authenticated attacker creates a ₹10,00,000 donation row (create-order), then calls /donations/verify with the victim donationId plus a VALID Razorpay signature for the attacker's OWN small order (e.g. their own ₹101 test order). The signature verifies because it is a genuine Razorpay HMAC over (attacker_order_id|attacker_payment_id) — the verify code never checks that attacker_order_id equals the donation row's razorpay_order_id. The victim donation row flips to status='paid', a real 80G receipt PDF is emailed, and Razorpay only ever captured ₹101 from the attacker. Because there is also no ownership check, any logged-in user can verify ANY other user's donation. Net effect: large tax-deductible receipts minted for ~₹0; revenue fraud + 80G compliance fraud.
repro: 1) Attacker logs in, POST /donations/create-order {gaushalaId:X, amountInr:1000000} -> donationId=D (status created, razorpay_order_id=O_big). 2) Attacker separately creates+pays a tiny real Razorpay order O_small (₹101) and captures razorpay_payment_id=P_small + signature S_small (valid HMAC over O_small|P_small). 3) Attacker POST /donations/verify {donationId:D, razorpay_order_id:O_small, razorpay_payment_id:P_small, razorpay_signature:S_small}. Backend computes expected=HMAC(O_small|P_small)==S_small -> sigOk=true. Never compares O_small to D.razorpay_order_id. UPDATE donations SET status='paid' WHERE id=D. 80G receipt for ₹10,00,000 emailed. Attacker paid ₹101.
suggestedFix: Mirror consultation.ts exactly: (a) load userId=request.currentUser!.id and after fetching the donation row add `if (donation.user_id !== userId) return reply.code(403).send({ error: 'Not authorized for this donation.' });` (b) before signature compare add `if (body.razorpay_order_id !== donation.razorpay_order_id) return reply.code(400).send({ error: 'Order id mismatch.' });` (c) reject if donation.status==='paid' (idempotency, see PBO-10).

title: Temple donations silently mis-attributed as gaushala; temple_id never set; receipts name wrong entity
evidence: createOrderSchema (donations.ts:82-89) accepts only `gaushalaId` — no templeId field. INSERT (line 131-139) writes only `gaushala_id`, never `temple_id`: `INSERT INTO donations (id, user_id, gaushala_id, amount_inr, razorpay_order_id, status) VALUES (...)`. DonationForm.tsx:227-232 comment admits the hack: `// Backend expects 'gaushalaId' — we use it as the opaque cause id / for both gaushalas and temples; the backend stores it as a / string in the donations table.` and sends `gaushalaId: causeId` for BOTH kinds. Receipt generation (donations.ts:201-248) always looks up a gaushala profile: `const gaushalaProfile = await prisma.gaushalaProfile.findFirst({ where: { userId: donation.gaushala_id } })` then `gaushalaName: gaushalaProfile?.gaushalaName ?? 'Darshya Gaushala Network'` (line 244) and the email template (line 258) uses the gaushala name. schema.prisma:1166-1176 confirms donations is polymorphic with BOTH gaushalaId (String) and templeId (UUID FK) columns intended: `// Polymorphic donee. Exactly one of (gaushalaId, templeId) is non-null`.
impact: Every temple donation is stored with temple_id=NULL and gaushala_id=<temple cause id>. The 80G receipt PDF names 'Darshya Gaushala Network' (the fallback) instead of the actual temple, because no gaushala_profiles row matches a temple's cause id. Tax receipts misidentify the donee entity — donors claiming 80G for a temple gift get a receipt naming a gaushala, which can invalidate the deduction. Temple portal revenue reports (temple-portal.ts) which filter on donations.temple_id will show zero donations for every temple. Accounting/reconciliation splits donations across the wrong entity.
repro: Open a temple donation page (causeKind='temple'), donate ₹1100. Inspect the donations row: temple_id IS NULL, gaushala_id=<temple cause id>. Open the emailed 80G PDF: donee reads 'Darshya Gaushala Network'. Query temple portal donations: 0.
suggestedFix: Add `causeKind: z.enum(['temple','gaushala'])` + optional `templeId: z.string().uuid()` to createOrderSchema. When causeKind==='temple', INSERT temple_id (and leave gaushala_id NULL); when gaushala, current behavior. In verify, branch on which id is non-null to load Temple vs GaushalaProfile and render the receipt with the correct entity name + the temple's own 80G/PAN (add temple tax fields). Update DonationForm to send causeKind + the correct id field.

title: Booking wizard charges only base puja price; ₹51 platform + ₹150 prasad fees shown are never collected
evidence: page.tsx:115-116 `const PLATFORM_FEE = 51; const PRASAD_DELIVERY_FEE = 150;`. page.tsx:424-428 `const totalPrice = useMemo(() => { let total = basePrice + PLATFORM_FEE; if (wantsPrasad) total += PRASAD_DELIVERY_FEE; return total; }, [basePrice, wantsPrasad]);` — this is what is DISPLAYED. page.tsx:575-596 the create-order POST body sends `pujaSlug, templeOfferingId, scheduledDate, scheduledTime, devotees, sankalp, specialInstructions, prasadDelivery, deliveryAddress` — NO amount field at all. page.tsx:615 `amount = data.amount;` and page.tsx:627 `amount,` (Razorpay checkout opens with server-returned amount). Server side booking.service.ts:181-184 `const basePrice = offering.priceOverride ?? offering.pujaType.basePrice; const priceAmount = user.isNri ? offering.pujaType.nriPrice : basePrice;` — priceAmount is base price only, no fees. booking.service.ts:235 `priceAmount,` persisted. payment.service.ts:352 `const amountInPaise = Math.round(Number(booking.priceAmount) * 100);` — Razorpay order created for base price only. Button label page.tsx:1961 `Pay ₹{totalPrice.toLocaleString('en-IN')} with Razorpay` shows the fee-inclusive total while Razorpay charges only base.
impact: Revenue leakage of ₹51 per booking (+ ₹150 for every prasad booking) — the fees are advertised and consented to but never captured. For a ₹751 Satyanarayan Katha with prasad the user is shown ₹952 but Razorpay only charges ₹751; ₹201 lost per booking, scaled across all bookings. Also a display/charge mismatch: the pay button says ₹X but the Razorpay modal opens at ₹X-201, which erodes user trust and can cause abandonment. The tax invoice (pdf-invoice via payment.service.ts:35 amountInr=priceAmount) also shows the lower base amount, so the donor's receipt does not match the price they thought they agreed to. prasadDeliveryRequested is stored but the ₹150 prasad fee is never added to priceAmount anywhere server-side.
repro: Book any puja with prasad delivery on the wizard. Summary card shows ₹{base+51+150}. Click 'Pay ₹{total}'. Razorpay modal opens showing only ₹{base}. Complete payment. DB puja_booking.priceAmount = base; no fee ledger entry exists. Invoice PDF amount = base.
suggestedFix: Decide whether fees are real. If yes: in booking.service.ts createBooking add `priceAmount = basePrice + PLATFORM_FEE + (prasadDeliveryRequested ? PRASAD_DELIVERY_FEE : 0)` (and split platformCommission/priestPayout on the total or only the base per business rule — currently commission is 30% of priceAmount, so fees would also inflate priest payout 70%; likely fees should be platform-kept, so compute commission on basePrice and add fees as a separate non-commissioned line). Persist fee breakdown columns. If fees are NOT real, remove PLATFORM_FEE/PRASAD_DELIVERY_FEE from the display total so the button and modal match.

title: PATCH /bookings/:id has no ownership/role check; any authenticated user can drive any booking through the full state machine and inject arbitrary fields
evidence: bookings.ts:226-260 `server.patch('/:id', { preHandler: [authenticateUser] }, async (request, reply) => { const { id } = paramsWithId.parse(request.params); const body = updateBookingStatusSchema.parse(request.body); const updated = await bookingService.updateBookingStatus(id, body.status, body.data); return { booking: updated }; })` — request.currentUser is never read, no requireRole, userId never passed to the service. updateBookingStatus (booking.service.ts:261-298) signature is `(bookingId, newStatus, data?)` — no userId param, no ownership check, no role check; it only validates the state transition then `prisma.pujaBooking.update({ where: { id: bookingId }, data: { status: newStatus, ...data } })`. The route schema (bookings.ts:43-57) allows `data: z.record(z.any()).optional()` — arbitrary JSON merged into the update.
impact: Privilege escalation + data tampering on every booking. Any logged-in devotee can: (a) confirm their own unpaid booking without paying (PATCH status pending_payment->confirmed), bypassing payment entirely; (b) cancel/advance/complete any OTHER user's booking by id (transition it to cancelled, in_progress, completed, video_uploaded, delivered, or refunded) — the state machine in VALID_TRANSITIONS is the only gate; (c) inject arbitrary fields via `data` (e.g. {priestId: <attacker priest>, priceAmount: 0, platformCommission: 0, priestPayout: 999999, cancellationReason: '...'}) because `...data` is spread into the Prisma update with no allowlist. title: [NEW] Donation verify is not idempotent — double-verify mints a second 80G receipt number + second receipt email for one payment

title: [NEW] Puja verifyPayment has no caller-ownership check — any authenticated user with a valid signature can confirm any booking (asymmetric with store-order verify which IS owner-gated)

title: /api/v1/admin/cron/tick still accepts cron token as ?token= query param (legacy fallback) -> leaks secret into Render access logs + CDN caches
impact: PARTIAL fix since the prior audit: the timing-safe compare (timingSafeEqual) was added, closing the timing-oracle half of the original finding. However the query-param leak vector remains: a caller can still pass ?token=<CRON_AUTH_TOKEN> and it will be accepted. Query strings are logged verbatim in Render access logs, CDN/edge logs, and any upstream proxy logs, and may be cached by intermediary caches — so the cron secret can be disclosed via log access or cache exposure. The header path is safe; the query fallback is the residual risk.

suggestedFix: Remove the queryToken fallback entirely (accept x-cron-token header only). If an external free-tier pinger (UptimeRobot) cannot send headers, front it with a thin redirect/relay that injects the header, or rotate to a dedicated low-privilege token for the query path. At minimum, configure Render/CDN to strip/scrub the token query param from access logs and set Cache-Control: no-store on the response (currently none set).

title: /api/v1/astrology/horoscope/prewarm compares cron secret with plain !== (timing oracle) AND skips auth entirely when CRON_SECRET env is unset (default-allow)
impact: Two distinct problems vs the cron-auth middleware doctrine. (1) Timing oracle: `token !== cronSecret` (line 204) is a short-circuiting string compare that leaks the secret byte-by-byte via response timing, unlike the constant-time compare used everywhere else (cron-auth.ts, and the admin-leads tick handler that was hardened in PUB-03). (2) Default-allow: the `if (cronSecret)` guard (line 202) means if CRON_SECRET is missing/empty in any environment (misconfigured deploy, a Render env var that didn't propagate, a test/staging instance), the auth check is SKIPPED entirely and prewarmDailyHoroscopes() runs for ANY anonymous caller — the opposite of cron-auth's fail-loud default-deny. prewarmDailyHoroscopes likely fans out 12+ LLM/astrology computations (a cost/abuse vector, not just a data leak).
repro: If CRON_SECRET is unset on the instance: curl -X POST 'https://api.darshya.online/api/v1/astrology/horoscope/prewarm' (no headers) -> 200 { prewarmed: ... }. Timing attack: send repeated requests with progressively-correct token prefixes and measure response time differences (plain !== short-circuits on first differing byte).
suggestedFix: Replace the handler with the existing requireCronBearer middleware (or requireCronQueryToken) from middlewares/cron-auth.ts — it already implements constant-time compare AND default-deny (401 cron_auth_misconfigured when env unset). Add `{ preHandler: [requireCronBearer] }` to the route and delete the inline check. Ensure CRON_SECRET is set in every deployed environment.

title: NEW: /api/v1/semantic-search leaks unpublished/draft temples and content (no status filter) — unlike /api/v1/search and /api/v1/content which correctly filter

Vector path — raw SQL has NO status/isActive filter, scans every row with an embedding:

    from ${tableSql}
   where embedding is not null
   order by embedding <=> ${lit}::vector
   limit ${lim}   // lines 66-74 — no `where status='active'`/`status='published'`

LIKE fallback path — also no status filter on any of the three tables:
  prisma.contentItem.findMany({ where: { OR: [{ title: { contains: q, mode: 'insensitive' } }, { body: { contains: q, mode: 'insensitive' } }] }, select: {...}, take: limit })  // lines 89-94 — NO status:'published'
  prisma.temple.findMany({ where: { OR: [{ name: {...} }, { description: {...} }] }, select: {...}, take: limit })  // lines 108-113 — NO status:'active'
  prisma.pujaType.findMany({ where: { OR: [{ name: {...} }, { description: {...} }] }, select: {...}, take: limit })  // lines 127-132 — NO isActive filter

Compare the CORRECT pattern in /api/v1/search (search.ts):
  prisma.temple.findMany({ where: { OR: [...], status: 'active' }, ... })        // search.ts:33
  prisma.contentItem.findMany({ where: { OR: [...], status: 'published' }, ... }) // search.ts:73

And content.service.ts:
  const where = { status: 'published', ... }   // content.service.ts:30,198 ; findBySlug: if (!item || item.status !== 'published') return null // line 104
impact: Logged-out users can discover pending_review temples, draft/unpublished content items, and inactive puja types via /api/v1/semantic-search — entities that are correctly hidden from /api/v1/search and /api/v1/content. A draft blog/article exposing unreleased features, a pending_review temple with unverified/PII-laden description, or a deactivated puja can all be surfaced by semantic query. This is an inconsistency that turns the semantic endpoint into a draft-content oracle. Secondary: the vector path calls generateEmbedding() (a Cohere API billable call) on every request with only the global 100/min/IP rate limit (no tightened per-route cap in server.ts:162-181 for /semantic-search), so anonymous abuse drives LLM spend.
repro: curl 'https://api.darshya.online/api/v1/semantic-search?q=<term-matching-a-draft>&kind=all' -> hits include draft content_items (status<>'published') and pending_review temples (status<>'active') that /api/v1/search?q=<same> correctly excludes.
suggestedFix: Add status filters to BOTH paths in semantic-search.ts: vector path -> append `and status='active'` (temples) / `status='published'` (content_items) / `is_active=true` (puja_types) to the raw SQL per table (requires per-table SQL branch since columns differ); LIKE fallback -> add `status: 'published'`/`status: 'active'`/`isActive: true` to each findMany where. Also add a tightened rate-limit policy for url.startsWith('/semantic-search') in server.ts onRoute hook (e.g. max: 20/min) to cap embedding API spend.
